BiblicalUsage: Chabal in Aramaic means to ruin or destroy, and Daniel uses it for the kingdoms of this world. God will destroy any king who lifts a hand against His house, He will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, the great tree will be cut down and destroyed, and yet Daniel himself was not hurt — the lions could not destroy a man God had kept.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the kingdoms that destroy are themselves destroyed, and the kingdom that cannot be destroyed belongs to the God of heaven. That is the whole story of Daniel in one word.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
